variant_decisions.evidence: Qere וּֽצְפוּנְךָ֮ and ketiv וצפינך differ only in the vowel letter (waw vs yod) of the same root צפן with 2ms suffix; both yield 'thy hidden store / thy treasure' with the same syntax and the same 'and' conjunction. ASV 'And whose belly thou fillest with thy treasure' renders that sense without preferring either spelling, and neither ASV note bears on this unit — both are classed alternative_rendering and concern the wording of 'men who are thy hand' and 'whose portion in life', not the reading here. Nothing in the English excludes either candidate, so both remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
